theme: Cana; Temple cleansing; Nicodemus, born again
readingInstruction: Read John 2:1-3:36. Jesus turns water into wine at Cana, cleanses the temple, and talks with Nicodemus at night. John the Baptist then speaks of Jesus’ increase. Notice that John calls miracles “signs,” pointing to something beyond themselves.
settingTheScene: John does not record Jesus’ birth or temptation. After the prologue and the first disciples, he moves to a wedding in Cana of Galilee. Jesus’ first sign is there. Then he goes to Jerusalem for Passover, clears the temple, and meets a ruler of the Jews, Nicodemus, who comes by night. John 3:16 comes from this conversation and has been called the gospel in a sentence. It is also the anchor verse of this unit.
observation: “This, the first of his signs, Jesus did at Cana in Galilee, and manifested his glory. And his disciples believed in him” (2:11).
“Destroy this temple, and in three days I will raise it up” (2:19).
“Truly, truly, I say to you, unless one is born again he cannot see the kingdom of God” (3:3).
“The wind blows where it wishes, and you hear its sound, but you do not know where it comes from or where it goes. So it is with everyone who is born of the Spirit” (3:8).
“For God so loved the world, that he gave his only Son, that whoever believes in him should not perish but have eternal life” (3:16).
“He must increase, but I must decrease” (3:30).
“Whoever believes in the Son has eternal life; whoever does not obey the Son shall not see life, but the wrath of God remains on him” (3:36).
interpretation:
At the wedding in Cana, the wine runs out, a serious embarrassment. Mary tells Jesus, and then tells the servants, “Do whatever he tells you.” Jesus has them fill six stone jars, used for Jewish purification, with water, and the water becomes wine, better than what was served before. John says this was the first of Jesus’ signs and “manifested his glory.” The abundance of wine, perhaps 120 to 180 gallons, points to the messianic age, which the prophets described as a feast of wine. The old purification is replaced by the new joy.

In Jerusalem, Jesus drives out the sellers from the temple. When asked for a sign, he says, “Destroy this temple, and in three days I will raise it up.” John explains that he was speaking about the temple of his body. Jesus is the true place where God and man meet, and he will rise on the third day.

Nicodemus, a Pharisee and a member of the council, comes at night. He recognizes that Jesus is a teacher from God. Jesus replies abruptly: “Unless one is born again he cannot see the kingdom of God.” Nicodemus is puzzled. How can anyone enter the womb a second time? Jesus explains that one must be born of water and the Spirit. The Spirit, like the wind, is sovereign and invisible but his work can be seen. A teacher of Israel should have known this from Ezekiel 36. Jesus then says that as Moses lifted up the serpent in the wilderness, so the Son of Man must be lifted up, that whoever believes in him may have eternal life.

Then comes verse 16. God’s love is the source. The world is the object, the whole sinful world. The gift is his only Son. The condition is belief, and the result is that we do not perish but have eternal life. The next verse says God did not send his Son to condemn the world, but that the world might be saved through him.

The chapter closes with John the Baptist, who rejoices that Jesus is gaining followers. He is the friend of the bridegroom. “He must increase, but I must decrease.” The one who comes from above is above all. And verse 36 sets the choice before everyone: believe and live, or reject and remain under wrath.
connection: Isaiah 25:6 and Amos 9:13-14 promise abundant wine in the age to come. Psalm 69:9 is the zeal for the house that the disciples recall. Malachi 3:1 promises that the Lord will suddenly come to his temple. Ezekiel 36:25-27 describes the cleansing and the new heart. Numbers 21:4-9 is the bronze serpent. Romans 5:8 and 1 John 4:9-10 echo God’s love in giving his Son. Ephesians 2:8-9 says we are saved by grace through faith.
application:
Memorize John 3:16 this week. It is the memory verse for the unit.

Say “He must increase, but I must decrease” as a prayer at the start of your day.

Think of a Nicodemus in your life, a thoughtful person with questions, and pray for them.
prayerPrompts: Thank Jesus for revealing his glory.
Thank him for the new birth, and ask him to keep working in you.
Tell him you believe, and ask him to deepen it.
